text:
sarah-support: Customer (acme-inc) hitting JSON.parse error in structured-streaming mode. They get `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` after ~18s of streaming on long responses. They attached their client log and said the stream abruptly stops mid-object.

sarah-support: Customer curl repro (they provided):
```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx\" \\
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-large&mode=structured > out.ndjson
```
They then do `tail -n 1 out.ndjson | jq .` and get the parse error.

sarah-support: Example tail from their file (last 240 bytes):
```
...,"choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":{"type":"json","value":{"order":{"id":12345,"items":[{"sku":"A1","qty":2}],"total":49.98},"meta":{"partial":true}}}}]
```
(note: missing closing `}}]}` — stream cut off mid-suffix)

tom-support: Any request_id or logs we can look up?

sarah-support: Request id 01H4ZQ9A2B3CXTJ7R4M6P0GQ (customer timestamp 2026-03-16T14:02:11Z). They said this happens intermittently on longer outputs.

raj-eng-runtime: Thanks. Two guesses: (1) a proxy/edge (customer -> cloud) or our gateway is closing the connection mid-chunk, or (2) streaming layer hit a keepalive/idle cutoff and sent FIN without final chunk. Can you paste our ingress log lines around that request_id?

sarah-support: Pasted from access logs (redacted):
```
[2026-03-16T14:02:11.123Z] req=01H4ZQ9A2B3CXTJ7R4M6P0GQ path=/v1/streams method=POST status=200 bytes_sent=18372 dur=18123ms upstream_status=200 upstream_bytes=18372 upstream_dur=18120ms conn_close=false
[2026-03-16T14:02:29.512Z] req=01H4ZQ9A2B3CXTJ7R4M6P0GQ tcp_reset=1 note=upstream_connection_reset
```
(looks like connection reset ~18s after start)

maria-eng-sre: That tcp_reset=1 smells like proxy in the path (customer or our LB) dropping connection. Need to confirm if this is client-side NAT timeout or Cloud provider load balancer. Customer on AWS ELB?

sarah-support: Customer says they run requests from within their GCP VPC (GCLB) and sometimes from their user's browsers behind Cloudflare. They see it in both places.

leo-eng: Two actionable probes: (A) reproduce with long running stream from our staging using `tc` to simulate small MTU / chunk splits; (B) create an internal s2s curl that forwards via customer-like proxy to see if chunk boundary leads to truncation. I can run A quickly.

raj-eng-runtime: Also check whether our streaming code ever emits partial JSON events (we send chunked SSE with fragments) — if a chunk boundary separates the final braces and the client or intermediary buffers drop it, they'd end up with invalid JSON. We should instrument to always flush final suffix as its own event.

maria-eng-sre: I'll search edge logs for other `tcp_reset=1` spikes around that hour and correlate with LB autoscaler events. If LB is recycling backend connections at ~18s window that's suspicious.

tom-support: Customer asked for a workaround in the meantime. Suggestion: switch to non-streaming structured mode (full response) or add a retry on parse failure that re-requests remainder with small prompt context? They don't want to abandon streaming.

sarah-support: Shared those workarounds. Customer wants us to try an internal repro and confirm if this is on our side before they change infra.

raj-eng-runtime: Action items:
- leo to run MTU/chunk-split probe and post raw bytes we emit (chunk boundaries).
- maria to check LB/edge reset patterns for that request_id window.
- I'll add temporary debug logging to the streaming path to emit final-stream-suffix markers (flag) for a short rollout on staging and prod (canary).

deploy-bot: Scheduled ramped canary for streaming-debug-flag on prod at 2026-03-17T01:00:00Z (20% hosts) — ci/1234

sarah-support: Thanks — I'll update the customer and request they keep a sample output file if it happens again. Also asked them to confirm if they use HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 and whether any proxy resets show up on their side.

leo-eng: Running MTU probe now, will post sample raw chunks in this thread shortly.

sarah-support: Appreciate it. I'll keep this thread open and escalate if we see a pattern across customers.
